en: Taal Volcano sits on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake, which itself is located on the island of Luzon.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season, making them look like giant chocolate mounds.
The mossy forests on Mount Pulag in Benguet are covered in thick, green moss and frequent fog.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows underground through a massive cave before emptying into the sea.
The Hundred Islands National Park in Pangasinan contains over a thousand small islands formed from ancient coral reefs.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila connects the large Laguna de Bay directly to the Manila Bay.
The Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea are isolated coral atolls that host hundreds of marine species.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountain slopes and fed by mountain streams.
The giant Rafflesia flower, found in the rainforests of Mindanao, blooms with five thick, reddish-brown petals.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its own brain.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical, cone-shaped profile visible from miles away.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features crystal-clear, deep blue freshwater emerging from an underwater cave.
